questions.prompt: How does belief differ from truth?
questions.answer: Belief is an attitude; truth concerns whether the proposition is actually the case.
questions.feedback: Check the definition and explain it in your own words before retrying.

questions.prompt: Can a justified belief be false?
questions.answer: Yes; reasonable grounds may be misleading.
questions.feedback: Check the distinction or calculation against the worked case; correct the first unsupported step.

questions.answer: They challenge whether justified true belief alone is sufficient for knowledge.
questions.feedback: State a concrete implication or limitation and retry without notes.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Distinguishes belief, truth and justification and recognises epistemic luck.
scoring.transfer: Build an epistemic audit of three fictional propositions, separating belief, evidence, actual status and possible epistemic luck. Include a claim whose truth remains unresolved.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
